source_references.title: AI-enabled agents improve patient care access at RUSH: PwC

business_problem: Rush needed to make patient access less fragmented across calls, messages, and web channels while reducing the heavy administrative burden on clinicians and staff handling routine requests.
solution_summary: Rush and PwC rebuilt patient access around Salesforce Health Cloud, Data 360 (Data Cloud), and AI agents so routine requests no longer have to bounce between disconnected channels and teams. PwC aligned patient data across clinical and non-clinical systems, connected the contact center to electronic health record workflows, and moved the experience from legacy IVR menus to intent-based telephony and self-service across calls, messages, and websites. AI agents now answer common questions, handle prescription-refill and provider-lookup requests, and surface patient history, preferences, and next steps in one place for staff. The implementation was paired with an AI governance framework that intakes, monitors, evaluates, and improves use cases so new automations remain ethical, explainable, and scalable. That architecture lets Rush reserve human capacity for higher-acuity patient needs while making access faster and more consistent.

solution_components.name: Salesforce Health Cloud
solution_components.role: Provides the patient-engagement and workflow foundation for Rush’s connected access experience.

solution_components.name: Data 360 (Data Cloud)
solution_components.role: Aligns clinical and non-clinical patient data so staff and automations work from shared context.

solution_components.name: AI agents
solution_components.role: Handle routine patient questions and self-service requests across channels before escalating complex cases.

solution_components.name: AI governance framework
solution_components.role: Controls intake, monitoring, evaluation, and continuous improvement of AI use cases across Rush.

data_flow: Patient questions and access requests arrive through calls, messages, and websites, then AI agents use context aligned in Health Cloud and Data Cloud to answer routine needs, support self-service, and surface next steps. When cases are complex, workflows connect the contact center and EHR systems so staff can pick up with patient history and context in one place.
business_outcome: Rush reduced routine patient-call volume, accelerated responses to common questions, increased use of digital self-service, and freed staff and clinicians to spend more time on complex care interactions.
metrics: 15% drop in patient calls for routine requests
5-15% faster responses to common patient questions with agentic AI
25% more patients used digital tools to get care info—avoiding call center wait times
clinicians spent up to 40% of their time on administrative tasks before the redesign
architecture_clues: The program connected clinical and non-clinical data into one patient-access workflow.
Rush moved from Interactive Voice Response (IVR) to full intent-based telephony experiences and self-service across channels.
Staff can view patient history, preferences and next steps in one place.
An AI governance framework monitors and continuously improves candidate AI use cases.
evidence_quotes: Working with PwC, we wanted to build a connected experience enabled by Salesforce Health Cloud, Data 360 (Data Cloud), Marketing.

PwC helped design the blueprint, align patient data across clinical and non-clinical systems and build workflows that connect everything—from the contact center to the electronic health record (EHR) systems.
Now, AI agents handle high-volume requests—like prescription refills, clinic hours and provider lookups—giving patients quick answers without tying up staff.
Alongside implementing Salesforce solutions, PwC also helped Rush establish an AI governance framework that confirmed responsible innovation and scalable impact.
Smarter strategy and AI-enabled agents helped reduce calls by 15%— for faster, more personal care.
